hooks.command: echo 'BLOCKED: EnterWorktree places worktrees inside .claude/worktrees/, nested in this repo tree, where whole-tree tooling (prek, test discovery, search) would walk another agents in-flight code. Run git worktree add ../adept-worktrees/<branch> and cd there instead.' >&2; exit 2

ISO=$(jq -r '.tool_input.isolation // empty'); if [ "$ISO" = "worktree" ]; then echo 'BLOCKED: Agent isolation "worktree" places the worktree inside .claude/worktrees/, nested in this repo tree. Have the dispatched agent run git worktree add ../adept-worktrees/<branch> and cd there as its first step instead.' >&2; exit 2; fi

TO=$(jq -r '.tool_input.to // empty'); [ -z "$TO" ] && exit 0; case "$TO" in team-lead | main) exit 0 ;; esac; D="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/adept-probe-budget"; mkdir -p "$D" || exit 0; F="$D/$(printf '%s' "$TO" | tr -c '[:alnum:]._-' '_')"; NOW=$(date +%s); if [ -f "$F" ] && [ $(( NOW - $(cat "$F" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) )) -lt 900 ]; then echo "BLOCKED: this worker's probe budget is already spent. references/dispatch-liveness.md allows ONE probe per worker per run. No reply proves nothing -- a worker inside a long tool call answers at its next turn boundary, not on demand -- so a second probe buys the same non-answer at the price of a full dispatcher turn. The wait is already a hold: record it in the workflow's run report or ledger, drain other work, and wait on the harness end-of-run notification or a single background task. If this is a genuine non-probe message (a branch refresh, an answer to a question the worker asked), wait out the window or clear "$D"." >&2; exit 2; fi; printf '%s' "$NOW" > "$F"; exit 0
